expectations.text: Answers the question of what a team is missing in functions rather than in people
expectations.evidence: The transcript keeps functions and headcount apart: "The guide says keep functions and headcount separate". It uses a table of three functions plus one shared duty, and it says what matters is that "these three jobs get done by someone". It also includes "Missing a function? Say so when you join a team". It explicitly rejects "One person per slot" and says a four-person team doesn't "need a fourth function."

expectations.text: Answers the question of what a team is missing in functions rather than in people
expectations.evidence: The slot table describes each role by what it covers (back end and data, front end and mobile, UX, product direction). Missing capacity is still counted in people, though. The rules say "One person per slot" and "All four slots filled", and the incomplete-team section says "We'll help you find people for the open slots." Only the closing note leans toward functions, with "teams of up to four who cover all four roles", and it offers that as an optional alternative. The answer never asks which function a team cannot cover, so the gap is still framed as headcount.
